strengths: The severe editorial typography, restrained palette and unusually generous space give the bureau an intelligent, principled voice appropriate to difficult institutional work.
Project scale is expressed through unequal image sizes and placement on desktop, turning the 55× range into a meaningful portfolio hierarchy rather than a uniform card grid.
The architecture photography is consistently atmospheric and materially focused, with strong crops that support the conversion-and-repair positioning.
Repeated typographic, spacing, rule and footer treatments make the pages feel like one deliberate system.
Specific facts, project descriptions, people, recognition and the admission that the bureau sometimes advises against proceeding create unusual credibility.

defects.detail: The paid two-week condition survey is the commercial entry point, but it is buried in bureau copy. Generic Contact links do not explain what a prospective client should send, what happens next or why the survey is the appropriate first commitment.

On the supplied mobile work sequence, projects collapse into a largely uniform single-column procession. The desktop hierarchy communicates which work matters through scale, but much of that opinion disappears on mobile.
The referenced home mobile renders were unavailable, so the responsive quality of the most compositionally complex page cannot be fully verified.
Several desktop sections use such large vertical intervals that related headings, explanations and project groups risk feeling disconnected rather than purposefully paced.

The photographs are well chosen, but their visual authority can momentarily imply authorship of the buildings; the small-print attribution is ethically adequate yet not prominent enough to eliminate that first-glance ambiguity.
The unequal desktop portfolio lands as the signature idea, but its force is weakened when mobile presentation gives projects substantially more equal visual weight.

summary: This is distinctive, disciplined professional work with an unusually strong match between editorial form and the bureau's anti-demolition position. It needs a clearer condition-survey pathway and a mobile composition that preserves the portfolio's deliberately unequal hierarchy before it fully serves the commercial brief.
